# Elementary sanity only

The first request constrains a single relative port bias to [2,4] ps. Its tight
upper differences are4 and-2; each direction has one witnessing constraint.
The second request has one always-anchored endpoint and no links or drift, so its
periodic bound, age and peak are0, and the smallest safe setting is0.

These two requests do not cover inconsistent profiles, inferred multi-hop
calibration, nontrivial clock propagation, delayed application, heating, outages,
intermittent anchors, guard-dependent reachability, warmup, audit or packet replay.
Those requirements and the size domain are fully specified in the public docs.
=== requests ===
{"op":"calibrate","profile":{"groups":2,"jitter_ps":[1,2],"measurements":[[0,1,2,4]]}}
{"op":"plan","profile":{"groups":1,"jitter_ps":[0],"measurements":[]},"fabric":{"n":1,"interval_ns":10,"slice_ns":10,"offset_ns":5,"drift_ppb":[0],"heat":[],"anchors":[[0,0,1]],"links":[],"slices":[[]],"blackouts":[],"guards_ns":[0,1],"reconfig_ns":0}}
=== expected ===
{"status":"ok","upper_ps":[[0,4],[-2,0]],"pred":[[null,0],[1,null]]}
{"status":"ok","profile":{"status":"ok","upper_ps":[[0]],"pred":[[null]]},"period_rounds":1,"peaks_as":[0,0],"guard_ns":0,"bounds_as":[[0]],"age_rounds":[[0]],"pred":[[null]],"warmup_cycle":0}
